articles.body: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' continued its strong run at the box office on Day 20. The film, which saw its collections dip on Monday, recorded good growth at the ticket windows on its third Tuesday at the box office.'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' box office collection Day 20As per a report on Sacnilk, the Tom Holland-led superhero film recorded an estimated Rs 2.55 crore net collection in India and a gross total collection of Rs 2.98 crore across 3,317 shows on its 20th day.Its total India net collection has now reached approximately Rs 471.70 crore, while its India gross collection stands at Rs 563.92 crore.With this, the Hollywood film is now the second-highest-grossing film of 2026 in India.'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' crosses USD 2 billion worldwideThe film has also achieved a major milestone at the global box office, crossing the USD 2 billion mark, with an estimated global haul of USD 2.03 billion. 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' has now become the first film in the franchise to cross the coveted milestone.The film has also recorded one of the fastest USD 2 billion runs in box office history, reaching the milestone in just 20 days. This makes it the second-fastest film ever to cross the USD 2 billion mark, behind only 'Avengers: Endgame', which achieved the feat in 11 days.Other films like 'Ne Zha 2' took 33 days to reach the milestone, while 'Avatar: The Way of Water' and 'Avatar' took 39 and 47 days, respectively.The film's current worldwide total is estimated at USD 794 million from the domestic market and USD 1.23 billion from international territories.'Brand New Day' eyes 'Avengers: Infinity War' recordWith its worldwide collection currently estimated at USD 2.03 billion, 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' is now around USD 20 million away from overtaking 'Avengers: Infinity War', which finished its theatrical run with approximately USD 2.05 billion.If it crosses that mark, the Tom Holland-starrer would become the second-highest-grossing Marvel film worldwide, behind 'Avengers: Endgame', which earned approximately USD 2.80 billion globally.The film has already surpassed the previous worldwide record held by 'Spider-Man: No Way Home' which earned approximately USD 1.92 billion worldwide.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Inside Vivek Oberoi’s Mumbai home where Goan farmhouse aesthetics, family heirlooms and pet cow Kamadhenu create rustic retreat
articles.summary: Vivek Oberoi has created a peaceful home in Mumbai that feels far removed from the city's usual hustle and bustle. Designed around the warmth of a coz.
articles.body: Vivek Oberoi has created a peaceful home in Mumbai that feels far removed from the city's usual hustle and bustle. Designed around the warmth of a cozy Goan farmhouse, his residence brings together timeless antique furniture, natural elements, greenery and a few unusual touches, including a pet cow named Kamadhenu.In 2024, the actor warmly offered viewers a rare glimpse of his home through Urban Company's Reels to Rooms, revealing how the space reflects his personality as well as his life with wife Priyanka Alva.A home that feels like a village retreatVivek began the tour by introducing Kamadhenu, who has become an integral part of the unusual setup. For him, having a cow around the property helps recreate the atmosphere of a village despite living in Mumbai.“This is more her house than mine. The aroma of a cowshed gives you a feel that within this city, you are living in your own little village,” he said.The actor also explained that he wanted his personal space to be a contrast to his professional life. While his work requires him to inhabit fictional characters, home is where he can simply be himself.“I work in a world of make belief where everything is superficial but when I walk back from the world to my home, I am not the actor Vivek Oberoi, I am just me,” he said.Goan influence runs through the interiorsWooden furnishings, ornate chandeliers, indoor plants and a large portrait of Goddess Lakshmi contribute to the property's distinctive aesthetic. Rather than opting for a polished, contemporary look throughout, Vivek and Priyanka chose elements that gave the interiors a more earthy and lived-in character.Vivek said sustainability and their connection to Goa were important considerations while designing the house.“The idea was that this home should come from me and Priyanka, and what it represents is our life. When we bought this house, we wanted it to reflect Goa. Everything that you see outside, inside is the essence of a farmhouse,” he said.An antique bed with family memoriesThe bedroom houses several antiques that Vivek has collected over the years, but one particular piece holds a much deeper emotional value. The vintage bed belonged to Priyanka's family and has been passed down through generations.“This bed has been in Priyanka’s family for half-a-century and maybe even longer than that. So, I love it because my earliest memory as a 4-year-old is sleeping in a bed like this and feeling cozy and secure while listening to stories from my dadi,” he said.The furniture and decor give the home a sense of history, while the surrounding greenery ensures that nature remains a visible part of the interiors.Embracing imperfectionsOne of the defining features of Vivek's home is its attempt to blur the boundary between the outdoors and indoors. Large windows bring views of tall trees into the living spaces, creating a connection with nature.The backyard continues the same philosophy, with exposed pipes and a visible tap becoming part of the space rather than being hidden away. Vivek said he enjoys these unconventional details instead of trying to make every corner look perfectly finished.“We like this quirkiness and madness,” he said while wrapping up the tour.Vivek has appeared in several popular Hindi films, including ‘Saathiya’ and ‘Omkara’, among other projects.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Suresh Oberoi recalls 2004 BJP stint; says Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Yogi Adityanath are ‘fine’, calls himself RSS, Mohan Bhagwat fan, but adds, ‘most people were simply interested in making money’
articles.summary: Veteran actor Suresh Oberoi recently and candidly opened up about his brief association with politics, his admiration for RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and .
articles.body: Veteran actor Suresh Oberoi recently and candidly opened up about his brief association with politics, his admiration for RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and his personal views on protests and activism. In a recent insightful conversation with Nidhi Vasandani on her popular YouTube channel, Oberoi recalled how he was introduced to the BJP in 2004 and spoke about meeting senior political figures, including L K Advani and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.Suresh Oberoi also explained why he eventually lost interest in active politics and spoke about his continuing admiration for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.Suresh Oberoi recalls joining BJP in 2004Speaking about his decision to explore politics, Oberoi said it was a college friend from Hyderabad who first suggested that he join the BJP.“I had a friend from my college in Hyderabad. One day, he came home and said, ‘This is the BJP. You should join it.’ This was in 2004,” Oberoi recalled.He said he accompanied his friend and was introduced to senior BJP leaders, including L K Advani and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.However, his political journey took a different turn after he met his guru, who strongly advised him against entering politics.“He gave me such a strong scolding. I had never seen him scold anyone like that in my life. He told me, ‘Be careful. Don’t ever go into politics and don’t even maintain contact with these people,’” Oberoi said.Despite initially continuing his association, Oberoi said he eventually felt uncomfortable with the political environment.Suresh Oberoi says actors should have researched before supporting CJP protests for NEET paper leak: 'Are they all students? You are responsible, before speaking, just understand'“I didn’t feel happy from within. My heart wasn’t in it. The vibrations didn’t feel right to me, and I didn’t feel good energy,” he said.‘I thought politics meant doing something for your country’Oberoi made it clear that his discomfort was not directed at every senior political leader. Referring specifically to Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and Yogi Adityanath, he said he was comfortable with some of the top leadership but did not connect with several people around them.“I’m fine with Modi ji, Amit Shah, Yogi ji and a few others, but with many of the people around them, I felt something was strange. It didn’t feel genuine to me,” he said.Explaining why politics eventually failed to hold his interest, Oberoi said his initial understanding of politics was very different from what he later observed.“I thought politics meant doing something for your country. Later, I realised that most people were simply interested in making money,” he said, while clarifying that he was not referring to everyone.‘I’m a fan of RSS, Mohan Bhagwat’Oberoi also spoke at length about Mohan Bhagwat, making it clear that while he admires the RSS chief, he is not formally associated with the organisation.“I have always been a fan of the RSS from within. I’m a fan of Mohan Bhagwat ji,” he said.The actor recalled inviting Bhagwat to his home and said the RSS chief eventually visited him for breakfast. Oberoi also shared an anecdote about his wife preparing halwa for Bhagwat.“He came home for breakfast. We were very happy. My wife makes very good halwa. We served it to him, and he really liked it,” he said.Oberoi said he remains in touch with Bhagwat and had spoken to him just a few days before the interview.However, he clarified that he has not formally joined the RSS. “I haven’t formally joined. I don’t attend the morning gatherings or participate in the parades carrying a stick,” he said.Suresh Oberoi questions narratives around protestsDuring the interview, Nidhi Vasandani asked Oberoi about the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests and the reactions from members of the film fraternity, including Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi.Oberoi said public figures should exercise caution before taking a strong position on an issue and should first establish the facts.“We are responsible people. The world listens to us and watches us. We have to think before speaking. We should research what is behind something, what the motive is and whose hand is involved,” he said.Referring to the NEET controversy, Oberoi questioned whether everyone participating in the protests was genuinely connected to the issue.“Are all of them NEET students? Are there politicians involved? Are there people throwing stones or creating chaos? We don’t know. Until you know the facts, how can you be so vocal about something?” he said.Oberoi added that he would rather admit that he does not know about an issue than comment without having researched it.“If I don’t know something, I won’t speak about it. I’ll simply say, ‘I don’t know about it,’” he said.Oberoi mentions Sonam Wangchuk while discussing activismThe actor was also asked about social activism and Sonam Wangchuk, whom Vasandani described as a social activist.Oberoi said he had seen similar movements and protests unfold before and questioned what they ultimately achieved.“I have seen all these people doing such things several times. Then everyone sits down peacefully. So what is all this? It is pointless,” he said.Asked whether he would personally participate in a protest or movement, Oberoi was unequivocal.“If someone came to me and said, ‘Suresh ji, come, let’s start a movement or protest,’ I would never go. Never,” he said.‘My work is acting’: Suresh Oberoi on activismOberoi said he believes his contribution should come through his profession rather than street protests or activism.“My work is acting. I will act. If someone says, ‘Suresh, let’s make a film, a video or a serial,’ yes, I can do that. But why should I become an activist?” he said.The actor also stressed that there are established institutions through which issues can be addressed.“We have the Supreme Court. There are people sitting there. Ministers are there. You have to put in some effort and find a solution,” he said.Oberoi strongly disapproved of violence during protests, particularly attacks on police personnel. He also referred to visuals of masked individuals attacking the police, saying such incidents made him question whether everyone involved was genuinely a student or protester.‘You should never give a strong opinion until you know the complete story’Oberoi concluded by reiterating his belief that people should not form opinions based on hearsay or isolated information.“You should never give a strong opinion until you know the complete story,” he said.The actor said that even things people see with their own eyes can sometimes be misunderstood without the complete context. He illustrated the point with a humorous example from films and television: “You see a man hugging a woman and later discover that she was actually his sister.”For Oberoi, the larger lesson was simple: research, verify and understand the context before speaking publicly. “I won’t listen until I have researched it and seen it myself,” he said.Meanwhile, Oberoi also spoke about the CJP protests for NEET paper leak and said that actors should have researched about it before supporting it. articles.body: Veteran actress Sharmila Tagore has said that the nation should stick to only the first two stanzas of the national song 'Vande Mataram'.The actress spoke with IANS on Thursday, and said that the entire song may not comply with the religious beliefs of many communities in India as they are monotheistic in nature.She told IANS, "My point of view is that there are many religious people who believe in one single God, not many Gods. In 'Vande Mataram', there is a stanza which says that many Gods are mentioned in 'Vande Mataram'"."It is difficult for those who believe in one religion to say, 'Vande Kali, Vande Durga'. Therefore, if we take all the religious people in India together, the first two stanzas are very good", she added.Actor Mukesh Khanna had also made a statement calling for the National Anthem to be replaced with 'Vande Mataram'.The actor claimed that the National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was written as a tribute to Queen Elizabeth.He earlier told IANS, "I have said this three years ago that 'Vande Mataram' should be made a national anthem.'Jana Gana Mana' is not the national anthem of our country. It is a tribute to Queen Elizabeth. Rabindranath Tagore wrote a song in praise of her. We have accepted it. Bhagyavidhata, Punjab, Sindh. It is not ours. 'Vande Mataram' is ours"."Lata ji sang it so beautifully. I had a meeting with Kalyanji Anandji bhai. It has been two years since I have read it. articles.title: Kangana Ranaut reacts to Sharmila Tagore's comment on 'Vande Mantaram': 'Shocked to see as an artist her views are so limiting, come out of Hindu Muslim mindset'
articles.summary: The debate over ‘Vande Mataram’ has resurfaced amid discussions about its place as India’s National Song and the difference between it and the Nationa.
articles.body: The debate over ‘Vande Mataram’ has resurfaced amid discussions about its place as India’s National Song and the difference between it and the National Anthem, ‘Jana Gana Mana’. The song, written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in the 1870s and featured in his novel Anandamath, the poem became a major rallying cry during India's freedom movement. The first two stanzas praise the physical beauty and landscape of the motherland. The later four stanzas explicitly invoke Hindu goddesses like Durga, Lakshmi, and Saraswati. The current debate centres largely on whether all of its verses should be treated alike, particularly because some later verses contain references to Hindu deities. While some argue that the song represents India’s spirit and the freedom struggle, others believe those references may be difficult for people from certain religious backgrounds to embrace.Veteran actor Sharmila Tagore recently shared her perspective on the matter, saying that people who believe in a single God may find some portions of the song difficult to accept. She explained that her concern was about bringing people of different faiths together. “My point of view is that there are many religious people who believe in one single God, not many Gods. In 'Vande Mataram', there is a stanza which says that many Gods are mentioned in 'Vande Mataram'”.Tagore added that the first two stanzas could be accepted more widely, while some of the later references could pose a problem for people following monotheistic faiths. “It is difficult for those who believe in one religion to say, 'Vande Kali, Vande Durga'. Therefore, if we take all the religious people in India together, the first two stanzas are very good”, she added.Sharmila’s comments soon drew a response from Kangana Ranaut. Sharing a video of the veteran actress’ interview on her Instagram Stories, Kangana said she appreciated Sharmila for expressing her reservations but questioned her interpretation of the song as an artist.“I appreciate that Sharmila ji has spoken about her reservation on Vande Mataram, but I am shocked as an artist how can her views on art/poetry can be so limiting and contrived, in any poetry or song words are metaphors, a poet or artist uses all kinds of imaginations draws unbelievable parallels to bring about the desirable effect, Vande Matram is the spirit of freedom struggle Bankim Chandra ji is compelling the nation to awaken the Shakti within, how can you reduce such a great piece of art to mere religious practice.”Kangana went on to argue that references to Shakti in poetry should be understood as expressions of strength rather than only as religious references. She invoked Swami Vivekananda’s famous words to make her point and urged people to look beyond religious divisions.She added, "Vivekananda famously said I need youth who are made of iron, bones of steel and veins in which runs thunderbolt, he was not giving weather forecast, he was simply demanding Shakti to rise, please come out of Hindu Muslim mindset even if we believe in one God doctors also call power Shakti, let's embrace each other like our own, I absolutely love you and don't mind a crushing hug like you always give me.”While ‘Jana Gana Mana’ is India’s National Anthem, ‘Vande Mataram’ holds the status of the National Song and has a significant place in the country’s history of independence.Give your child the gift of confidence! It was Sandeep's call."Pranay Reddy Vanga alleges Deepika Padukone asked for 10% profit shareAccording to Pranay, Sandeep had been in touch with Padukone for nearly a year and a half and was keen to cast her in the Prabhas-led film. He elaborated, "She demanded 10 percent from the film's profit. Soon after, everything went overboard. See, she can ask for anything. If we are willing to give, we can give. articles.title: Madhubala asked Kamal Amrohi to divorce his wife and be with her, unlike Meena Kumari, recalls Tajdar Amrohi: ‘There were stories about her relationships with others, including Dilip Kumar’
articles.summary: Madhubala’s life was marked by immense stardom as well as deeply painful relationships. She entered the film industry as a child artist in the early 1.
articles.body: Madhubala’s life was marked by immense stardom as well as deeply painful relationships. She entered the film industry as a child artist in the early 1940s and rose to prominence with the 1949 classic *Mahal*, directed by Kamal Amrohi. According to Amrohi’s son Tajdar, the filmmaker and the legendary actress fell in love while working on the film. However, their relationship eventually came to an end because Madhubala wanted Kamal to divorce his wife, Sayeda, and separate from his family.Tajdar opened up about his father’s relationship with Madhubala, which took place years before Kamal went on to marry actor Meena Kumari. Recalling the circumstances of their split, Tajdar said in an interview with Vickey Lalwani, “Madhubala, aapko ye bata doon, mujhe badi khushi hoti hai ye baat kehte hue ki probably Kamal is the only man who has worked with three most beautiful ladies of the Indian screen — the only man. Meena Kumari, that Tragedy Queen of India, the Venus of the Indian screen Madhubala, and the Dream Girl Hema Malini."When further asked if Kamal Amrohi and Madhubala were in a relationship, his son said, "Yes, this was before Meena Kumari ji. I won’t say he rejected or brok up, but got back, peeche ho gaye. Baba called it off." Giving the reason for their break-up, Tajdar revealed that Madhubala demanded that Kamal Amrohi divorced his wife and leave his children. He said, "Madhubala wanted my father to get to divorce my mother, which Meena ji did not demand. No, toh woh chahti thi ki Baba divorce karein."He said, "Madhubala wasn’t an ordinary heroine. She was a major star of her time, and she was so beautiful.” He also referred to the actress’s other much-discussed relationships, saying, “There were many stories of her relationships with others as well. It is well known that she was with Dilip Kumar.”He added further, "Toh unhone ajeeb demand rakhi, Madhubala ne. Baba ne mana kar diya. Unhone kaha ki main itne paise deti hoon. Badi heroine thi, producer bhi ho gayi thi, paisa bhi bahut tha. Ki main aapko itna paisa deti hoon. Aap itna paisa apni biwi ko de dijiye aur itna paisa aapke bachchon ko de dijiye aur unko life se hata dijiye. Life se hata dijiye. (She was a major star and a producer as well. She had lots of money too. She said, ‘I will give you x amount of money. You give this much to your wife and to your kids, and get them out of your life).”According to Tajdar, Kamal refused to compromise on his family. He recalled his father’s response: “My father told her, ‘We won’t meet from here on because I sell stories and dialogues, not my children and wife. You want me to leave my wife. That won’t happen. She is a woman of my family’.”Tajdar explained that his parents were related, with his mother being the daughter of Kamal’s maternal uncle. He also claimed that Madhubala was “disappointed” after the relationship ended. According to him, her father, Attaullah Khan, had initially “no objection” to the match because Kamal had become a prominent name following the success of *Mahal*.Tajdar further said his mother was unaware of the affair at the time. “My mother didn’t know about Madhubala. She just knew that Mahal was being made, and it was my father’s first directorial,” he recalled.Kamal Amrohi later married Meena Kumari, but his first wife, Sayeda, reportedly learned about the marriage through film magazines while she was living with their children in their village in Uttar Pradesh. In an earlier conversation with News18 Urdu, Kamal’s daughter Rukhsar recalled that her mother eventually encouraged the children to establish contact with Meena through letters. Over time, the children developed a close relationship with the actor and began affectionately calling her ‘Choti Ammi’.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: In 2012, Jackie Chan received a dragon-themed Embraer Legacy 650 private jet; here's a look inside
articles.summary: Discover the stunning features of Jackie Chan's dragon-themed Embraer Legacy 650 private jet, including its spacious cabin and cultural significance.
articles.body: Jackie Chan is known for his high-energy action films, impressive martial arts skills and decades-long career in international cinema. Away from the screen, the actor has also been associated with luxury aviation. In 2012, he took delivery of an Embraer Legacy 650, a business jet that turned heads with its dragon-inspired exterior and roomy three-zone cabin.This was no ordinary executive jet. Its custom design reflected Chan’s connection to Chinese culture, and its long range made it well suited to international travel. Some reports put its value at around $30 million, though Embraer has not confirmed that figure.How did Jackie Chan become associated with the Embraer Legacy 650?Chan's association with Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer began in October 2011, when the company announced him as its brand ambassador for Embraer Executive Jets. The partnership was intended to strengthen the manufacturer's presence in China and introduce its aircraft to a wider international audience.On February 3, 2012, Embraer announced the delivery of a Legacy 650 to Chan in São José dos Campos, Brazil. It was the first aircraft of this model delivered in China. The announcement also confirmed that Chan would help promote the company's executive aircraft globally.In the same announcement, Chan explained his choice of aircraft, highlighting its spacious three-zone cabin, quiet performance and luxurious interiors.A dragon-inspired exterior makes the jet distinctiveOne of the most eye-catching things about Chan’s Legacy 650 is its dragon-themed paint job. Bold red and yellow dragons sweep along the white fuselage, and Chan’s personal logo sits on the tail.The design carries cultural meaning too. In Chinese tradition, the dragon is an important symbol, often linked with strength, power and good fortune. It was a fitting choice for the aircraft, since 2012 was the Year of the Dragon in the Chinese zodiac.Embraer pointed this out in its delivery announcement, calling the dragon logo an auspicious start to the year. Rather than following the understated appearance of many private jets, this aircraft reflected Chan's identity and cultural background.Inside the Embraer Legacy 650: Three separate cabin zonesThe aircraft's interiors were designed around comfort and practicality. Its three-zone cabin allows passengers to use different sections for working, dining and relaxing during a journey.The Legacy 650 also features a fully equipped wet galley, an in-flight-accessible baggage compartment and technology designed to reduce cabin noise. These facilities make longer journeys more comfortable for passengers who need to work or rest while travelling.According to Embraer's published specifications, the Legacy 650 has a range of approximately 3,900 nautical miles, or 7,223 kilometres, with four passengers under specified flight conditions. Its Honeywell Primus Elite avionics suite is another feature of the aircraft's technical setup.Jackie Chan added another Embraer jet to his aviation portfolioChan's relationship with the manufacturer continued after the Legacy 650 delivery. In February 2016, Embraer announced that he had received the first Legacy 500 delivered to a customer in China.In its announcement, the company noted that the Legacy 650 had already provided Chan with convenient international travel. The actor also spoke about how the aircraft supported his acting assignments and philanthropic activities.The Legacy 500 and Legacy 650 sit in different classes of business jet, each with its own strengths and travel options.A private jet with a personal identityJackie Chan’s Legacy 650 stands out because it pairs executive-level comfort with a design that is unmistakably his own. Its dragon graphics, long-range capability and spacious cabin made it different from the conventional image of a luxury private jet.While its reported price may attract attention, the story behind the aircraft is equally interesting: a partnership between a global film star and an aviation manufacturer, brought together through a jet that reflects both modern engineering and Chinese cultural symbolism.Who is Jackie Chan?Jackie Chan is a Hong Kong-born actor, martial artist, filmmaker, stunt performer and producer who rose to international fame with his action-comedy films. He’s best known for blending martial arts with physical comedy and for doing many of his own stunts.His much-loved films include 'Drunken Master', 'Police Story', 'Rush Hour' and 'Shanghai Noon'. Over the years, he has built a worldwide following, and he’s also become known for his charity work and his efforts to promote Chinese culture.In August 2025, Jackie Chan received the Pardo alla Carriera or Career Leopard, at the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland, recognising his remarkable contribution to international cinema. The honour added another milestone to his celebrated career spanning more than six decades.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: SNL's "Sister" Sketch Is Hitting Home for Family Caregivers Who Do Everything
articles.summary: Jane Wickline stars in the viral November 14 pretape about women whose siblings are happy to let them take on everything.
articles.body:
Comedian John Mulaney 's seventh time hosting Saturday Night Live brought the fresh New York Musical many were hoping for — but the evening also delivered a less expected viral sketch. The pretaped "Sister" is a razor-sharp assessment of a dynamic common in many families: One in which everyone's all too happy to let a certain sibling handle every single aspect of caregiving for a loved one.

"My dad means the world to me. So when I noticed him start to slow down, I knew I needed to get him the best care possible," a man (Mulaney) says at the top of the parody ad. "I didn't want to put him in a nursing home, but a private health aide could cost thousands a week. I didn't know where to turn."

"That's when I heard about Sister," he adds, as an exhausted-looking woman with rolling luggage ( Jane Wickline ) is presented like a new medical product.

Jane Wickline plays the classic sister who caregiving always seems to fall on

"Sister is a live in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister," Mulaney's character narrates. "Now I don't have to worry about Dad getting the care and attention he needs, because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life and the stuf f I like to do."

"I love my mom more than anything. That doesn't mean I want to help her in the bathroom," another grown-man sibling (Andrew Dismukes) says in a testimonial, adding, "Sister doesn't either. But she will, whereas I won't."

There's no annoying paperwork or out-of-pocket fees with Sister. "Simply text 'Dad fell' to Sister and she will quit her job, break her lease, and move halfway across the country to take care of him," Mulaney's character explains.

A doctor (Mikey Day) breaks down how it works. "First, years of internalized sexism warps Sister's brain into thinking caretaking is her responsibility and somehow not yours," he says as a graphic featuring various religious symbols, books and television whirl around an animated woman. "Next, your text arrives, instantly activating her. And that's it! You're done for life. See you at the funeral."

A viewer called SNL's "Sister" sketch "so real it almost gave me a stroke from rage"

"Sister" racked up over 1.2 million views on YouTube alone in less than 24 hours after airing live. It was written by frequent collaborators Mikey Day and Streeter Seidell with Simon Rich, a former SNL writer who returned for Mulaney's episode, with "an assist" from Chase Rosenberg. "Dedicated to my sister Heidi," Seidell wrote on X (formerly Twitter).

"You have no idea how many daughters feel seen. Just spectacular," one fan replied to his post. Another wrote , "Brilliant from start to finish. Every single moment rang true for this oldest sister. But the fact that it has male writers behind it gives me hope for other people's brothers!"

Another simply replied, "Feels like you talked directly to my brothers."

SNL's YouTube comments were equally golden, with one person deeming it "one of the MOST wicked and spot on SNL sketches ever written." And one of the most-liked comments pulled no punches: "This was so real it almost gave me a stroke from rage."

articles.title: A Georgia O’Keeffe painting buried in a New York closet is going up for auction
articles.summary: The painting was buried behind coats and boxes in the closet of a Manhattan apartment for decades.
articles.body: NEW YORK — The painting was buried behind coats and boxes in the closet of a Manhattan apartment for decades. Few if anyone knew about the hidden treasure until the woman in her 90s who lived there nonchalantly told her niece one day, “oh by the way, there’s a Georgia O’Keeffe in the closet.” The painting — an early example from a time when O’Keeffe became enamored with the American Southwest — depicts a classic New Mexico landscape with rolling hills in earth tones. Christie’s estimates its value at $3 to $5 million. It is set to go up for auction on Tuesday. The auction house says the painting from 1930 was likely the first in a series of three. The second is in New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art. The other, for many years, was in the collection of the Rockefeller family. Up until now, the whereabouts of the first one had largely been a mystery. O’Keeffe painting comes from a key period The painting of Lobo Peak near Taos, New Mexico, is “particularly important because of its early date and its representation of the inception point of O’Keeffe’s time in the American Southwest,” said Tylee Abbott, director of American Art at Christie’s. In 1963, a New York art gallery sold the painting for $3,800 to a woman who gave it to her daughter. “Before that it was only known through photography that had been taken in 1931,” Abbott said. O’Keeffe, who died in 1986 at age 98, is often called the “Mother of American modernism.” She was a pioneer with her own style of abstract art, most known for paintings of flowers and Southwestern landscapes. She lived in Abiquiu, New Mexico, where she built a home and studio on land with breathtaking desert vistas that inspired the work of the 20th century painter. Many Native American communities trace their ancestry to the area in northern New Mexico. Family believes painting was a graduation gift The daughter of the woman who purchased the painting in 1963 kept it at her apartment in New York’s East Village, the auction house said. The family has asked the auction house not to release their identities. But they did share with Christie’s some details, including how the artwork was found. The woman who owned the painting lived into her late 90s before dying recently. Never married, she was extremely private and incredibly smart, the family said. At one point in her life, she worked with the U.S. Foreign Service, spending time in Europe. She collected antiques and abstract art but nothing close to the stature of the O’Keeffe. The family believes she received the painting as a graduation gift from her mother after earning a master’s degree in the 1960s. For many years, she displayed it until the mid-’80s when she noticed a guest looking at it a little too closely. Painting has O’Keeffe’s signature mark She boxed it back into the original packing crate and put it in the back of a closet, said her niece, who spent the last few years caring for her and spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity to honor the family’s request for privacy. Around 2022, the woman first mentioned to her niece that the painting was in the front closet. It stayed there until this year when they were cleaning out the apartment and getting her affairs in order. Once unboxed, it was obvious the painting was authentic. It has all the hallmarks of O’Keeffe’s work — including her signature marking on the back, a star with her initials “OK” scrawled in the middle.

articles.title: El 'shock' de Berto Romero al coincidir con su gran mito erótico: "Notas que hay una suciedad en tu mirada"
articles.standfirst: Se trata de Heather Graham y coincidió con ella en el Festival de Sitges
articles.summary: Se trata de Heather Graham y coincidió con ella en el Festival de Sitges
articles.body: Berto Romero ha sorprendido con una anécdota de esas que mezclan humor y vergüenza a partes iguales. El cómico, durante una nueva entrega de Nadie Sabe Nada, el programa que conduce junto a Andreu Buenafuente en la SER, recordó uno de los momentos más embarazosos que ha vivido: cuando conoció en persona a quien había sido su gran mito erótico durante años. El relato surgió al hablar de su reciente paso por el Festival de Cine de Sitges, donde presentó 5 minutos más, la película dirigida por Javier Ruiz Caldera y escrita por el propio Romero. El humorista no ocultó la ilusión que le hizo participar en un certamen al que guarda un cariño especial. "Le tenemos muchísimo cariño al festival de Sitges, que es el mejor festival de cine fantástico del mundo. Estábamos muy emocionados, además por aquello de ver y conocer a gente famosa. Yo, por ejemplo, me hice una foto con Heather Graham", señaló con toda intención. Porque Berto destapó uno de sus secretos... Confesó que aquel encuentro estuvo lejos de ser natural. Romero reconoció que los nervios y la admiración acumulada durante años le jugaron una mala pasada al encontrarse cara a cara con la actriz estadounidense. Entre risas, describió una sensación tan incómoda y difícil de ocultar cuando conoces a alguien por quien has sentido una fuerte atracción: "Notas que hay una suciedad en tu mirada", lo que provocó las carcajadas de Buenafuente. Heather Graham es una de las actrices más reconocibles de Hollywood de las últimas décadas. Tiene ahora 56 años. Su popularidad se disparó gracias a su papel de Rollergirl en Boogie Nights (1997), aunque alcanzó fama mundial interpretando a Felicity Shagwell en Austin Powers: La espía que me achuchó (1999). También ha trabajado para producciones como Drugstore Cowboy, Bowfinger, From Hell y Resacón en Las Vegas, además de dejar su huella en televisión con apariciones destacadas en la mítica serie Twin Peaks. Ahora, años después de aquel encuentro, Berto Romero sigue recordando con humor la vez que se quedó sin palabras delante de una de las mujeres que más admiró durante su juventud. Una escena tan incómoda como divertida que ha terminado convirtiéndose en una de las confesiones más comentadas de Nadie Sabe Nada.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh says, 'Ye Mahakal ki dharti hai' at Indore concert; adds, 'Kisi ke baap ka Hindustan thodi hai' as he reacts to restrictions on songs
articles.summary: Diljit Dosanjh told fans in Indore that nobody could keep him away from performing in the city, as he spoke about the curbs on his November 15 show, part
articles.body: Diljit Dosanjh told fans in Indore that nobody could keep him away from performing in the city, as he spoke about the curbs on his November 15 show, part of the Aura India Tour 2026. The singer also recited lines from a well-known ghazal by Rahat Indori.Diljit Dosanjh’s message to the Indore crowdA video from the concert, later posted by Diljit Dosanjh on Instagram, shows him telling a huge crowd that he had kept his promise to perform in the city despite the restrictions and warnings.On stage, Diljit said, “Yeh nahi gaana, woh nahi gaana. Yeh nahi kar sakte, woh nahi kar sakte. Dekho, ye Mahakal ki dharti hai aur yahan aane se humein koi rok nahi sakta. Na toh hum dare the pehle aur na darte hain aaj. Aur aap log kahan darte hain? Aap logon ki taqat hai jo aaj hum yahan hain. Jai Shree Mahakal (Don’t sing this song, don’t sing that song. You can’t do this; you can’t do that. Look, this is the land of Mahakal, and nobody can stop us from coming here. We were never afraid, and we aren’t afraid today either. And why should you be afraid? It is your strength and support that have brought us here today. Jai Shree Mahakal)!"The singer then read out a few lines from the late Urdu poet’s ghazal. He said, “Hamare munh se jo nikle wahi sadaqat hai, hamare munh mein tumhari zaban thodi hai. Agar khilaaf hai, hone do, jaan thodi hai, yeh sab dhuaan hai, koi aasmaan thodi hai. Main jaanta hoon ki dushman bhi kam nahi, lekin, hamari tarah hatheli pe jaan thodi hai. Sabhi ka khoon hai shaamil yahan ki mitti main, kisi ke baap ka Hindustan thodi hai (What comes out of our mouths is the truth; we don't speak with your tongue, after all. Let them oppose us if they wish; it's not as if our lives are at stake. All this is merely smoke; it's no vast sky, after all. I know we have no shortage of enemies either, but they don't put their lives on the line the way we do. The soil of this land bears the blood of everyone; Hindustan does not belong to anyone's father alone)."Why was the Indore concert restricted?The show took place after the District Child Protection Officer asked the venue management to make sure four of his songs were not played. The notice, dated November 6, came from the Women and Child Development Department. It listed ‘Patiala Peg’, ‘5 Taara’, ‘Jeeb Vicho Afeem’, also known as ‘Case’, and ‘Jatt Uthe Fire Karda’.Officials feared the lyrics could have “a wrong influence on young children." As children above five years were allowed to attend, the mall management was told to keep these tracks out of the set.What the Punjab and Haryana High Court saidThe notice cited a July 2019 order of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. While hearing cases mostly about noise pollution, the court had voiced concern over songs that promote alcohol, drugs and violence.The bench observed that the “glorification of the liquor, wine, drugs, and violence in the songs” across Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh “has increased in recent times.”It also said, "These songs affect the children of impressionable age." The court asked police chiefs to "ensure that no songs are played glorifying the liquor, wine, drugs and violence in any song even in live shows."Who filed the complaint against Diljit Dosanjh’s songs?The latest directive followed a complaint submitted on November 1 by Chandigarh-based professor Panditrao Dharenavar. He was also a petitioner in the 2019 case and wrote to the authorities seeking action against the four songs.Dharenavar asked that Diljit not perform the tracks “even with twisted lyrics”. In his complaint, he relied on the High Court order and the Centre’s campaigns against addiction.Diljit Dosanjh set for Coachella 2027Away from the controversy, Diljit Dosanjh is heading back to one of the biggest music festivals in the world. Four years after his Coachella debut, he has been named in the lineup for the 2027 edition. He will share the bill with global names such as Dua Lipa, Madonna, SZA and Tame Impala.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Grammys 2027 nominees: Raye, Rosalía and women artists dominate major categories
articles.summary: RAYE, Rosalía and women artists dominate Grammy 2027 nominees list
articles.body: Baby, where the hell is her Grammy? Female artists led the 2027 Grammy nominee list, which was unveiled during an early morning livestream Monday. The nominees were announced by a star-studded lineup of past Grammy winners and nominees, including Alan Menken, David Guetta and Pharrell Williams. Nominees across 100 categories were selected by 16,000 voting members of the Recording Academy. Eligible artists released their music during the period encompassing Aug. 31, 2025 — Aug. 28, 2026. The 69th Grammy Awards will take place at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Feb. 7. The show will air on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. Here are some of the key takeaways from this year’s announcement. Raye and Rosalía lead nominees British singer-songwriter Raye came out on top with a whopping 11 nominations, including for song, record and album of the year. The 28-year-old rose to the top of the charts this year with her hit, “Where Is My Husband!” She now joins Beyoncé in tying the record for the most nods earned by a female artist in a single year. Rosalía, who recently made history at the Latin Grammys by becoming the first female artist to win album of the year three times, snagged nine nominations. “LUX,” her fourth full-length album, features 13 different languages. Olivia Rodrigo snagged seven nods for her latest album “you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love.” Phoebe Bridges, Ella Langley and collaborator Miranda Lambert all also earned seven nominations apiece. Leaving space for ‘Wicked’ It may feel like an eternity ago that “Wicked: For Good” was released in theaters. But Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande notched a best traditional pop vocal performance nomination for their song “For Good,” from the sequel to the 2024 Broadway adaptation about an unlikely friendship between two witches. Erivo starred as the Wicked Witch of the West and Grande as the Good Witch, Glinda in the Universal Pictures film. (NBC News and Universal Pictures share Comcast as a parent company.) Erivo and Grande are no strangers to the Grammys, having won two Grammys and three Grammys, respectively. The film was also nominated in the best score soundtrack for visual media and best song written for visual media categories Dolly Parton receives posthumous nods The “Queen of Country” music, who died at age 80 in August, was among the nominees in the best country duo and group performance categories. Parton will also likely be heavily featured in the annual emotional in memoriam segment. Beyoncé earns her 100th Grammy nomination Queen Bey made history Monday with her 100th Grammy nomination for best R&B solo performance for her song, “MORNING DEW (DONK).” Beyoncé has won 35 Grammys in her storied career — the most of any female artist. Taylor Swift’s recognized for ‘Showgirl’ and ‘Toy Story’ Yes, Swift’s 12th album, “The Life of a Showgirl” came out over a year ago, and yes it still earned several nominations Monday morning. “Showgirl” took a spot in two of the three top categories, with lead single “The Fate of Ophelia,” earning a place for record of the year, and the album making the list of potential album of the year winners — an award Swift has won more than any other artist in her 20-year career. “Showgirl” also nabbed nominations for best remixed recording of “Opalite,” and for best pop duo/group performance for song “The Life of a Showgirl,” which features Sabrina Carpenter. The album, however, did not rise to a nomination for best pop vocal album. Swift also got two nominations for her single “I Knew It I Knew You,” which she wrote for “Toy Story 5” and released in June — including song of the year. Swift on Monday tied for the most song of the year nominations, with nine total throughout her career, including hits like “You Belong With Me,” “Blank Space” and “Anti-Hero.” Madonna makes a comeback Madonna received her first nominations in 16 years, since 2010, with “Bring Your Love.” The pop icon, 68, has won 7 Grammy Awards in her decades-long career. This year marked a comeback for the artist, who also performed at the MTV Video Music Awards for the first time in 23 years. There, she also took home three awards, including artist of the year. Oscar buzz starts now The best score soundtrack for visual media (includes film and TV) is typically stacked with Oscar contenders. This year was no different. Six-time Grammy-winning composer Ludwig Göransson scored two more nods Monday, for his work on two films: “The Odyssey” and “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.” Göransson has won three Oscars and is expected to be nominated again at Hollywood’s biggest night. Universal’s “The Odyssey,” which kicked off its Oscar campaign last week, is an expected front-runner in several categories for the Academy Awards. Daniel Pemberton’s “Project Hail Mary” score was also recognized. The Amazon MGM Studios film, which stars Ryan Gosling, is also among the buzzy Oscar contenders. The Grammy nomination marks a first for Pemberton. The score for “One Battle After Another,” from composer Jonny Greenwood, was also in the mix of this year’s nominees. The film won six Oscars at the 2026 Oscars. Swift’s “Toy Story” single, which received Recording Academy recognition, is also expected to be nominated at the Oscars next year. The pop star has already been busy campaigning for the song, with the Grammy nominations now helping fuel her to the top of the contender list.

articles.title: Richard Sterban, distinctive bass vocalist of The Oak Ridge Boys, dies at 83
articles.summary: Richard Sterban, a backup vocalist for Elvis Presley and the inimitable bass singer for The Oak Ridge Boys on their hit “Elvira,” died Saturday.
articles.body: Richard Sterban, a backup vocalist for Elvis Presley and the inimitable bass singer for The Oak Ridge Boys, died Saturday from complications of bronchitis and pneumonia after a battle with cancer. He was 83. “We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers,” his family said in a statement. “Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus.” Sterban joined The Oak Ridge Boys in 1972 after leaving his job as Elvis Presley’s backup vocalist, a press release states, citing Sterban’s desire to “be in the best vocal group in the world.” Fellow member of The Oak Ridge Boys, William Lee Golden, said Sterban’s death was a “sad day.” “GOD Bless and Comfort his Family through this Valley of Sorrow Rest in Peace my Friend,” he wrote on Facebook. The group won five Grammy Awards and four Academy of Country Music Awards, including Top Vocal Group and Album of the Year, and the prestigious Cliffie Stone Pioneer Award in 2008. It was inducted into the Gospel Music Hall of Fame in 2000 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2015. The Academy of Country Music said Sterban “helped shape one of country music’s most recognizable sounds” and said it was saddened by his death. “I grew up in radio hearing Richard’s voice come out of every speaker in America. That ‘oom-pa-pa-mow-mow’ on ‘Elvira’ was pure joy,” Academy of Country Music CEO Andy Schuon said in a statement. “He was a gentleman and a believer who carried gospel into country and pop, and brought millions of fans along with him.” Sterban, born on April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, developed his love for music at a young age. He started singing at 6 years old as a soprano in a Sunday school and as a tenor in his seventh-grade glee club. By the time he started eighth grade, his voice had dropped to bass. After graduating from Collingswood High School, Sterban studied music at Trenton State College, now The College of New Jersey. Sterban helped found the Keystones, a gospel quartet that tenor Joe Bonsall sang in. Bonsall was also a member of The Oak Ridge Boys. He died in 2024. Sterban’s path led him to sing in the Stamps Quartet, which Presley had hired to sing behind him. He performed with Presley for about a year and a half, until The Oak Ridge Boys called, in need of a bass singer. Sterban joined the group, replacing Noel Fox. Johnny Cash featured the group in his touring show and helped them sign to Columbia Records in 1973, but success did not come overnight, and their two albums drew little notice. While performing, the group caught the attention of music manager Jim Halsey, who convinced them to try country music. They later signed with Halsey, making hit after hit. “Y’all Come Back Saloon” reached No. 3 on the country chart in 1977 and “I’ll Be True to You” climbed to No. 1, the press release states. In 1981, the group released “Elvira,” which also hit No. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on the pop chart, sold more than two million copies, was named Single of the Year by both the Country Music Association and the Academy of Country Music, and won a Grammy Award. The group also performed for four presidents, from Gerald Ford to George W. Bush. Sterban is survived by his wife, Donna, and his five children.

articles.title: Apple TV is getting video podcasts you can watch for free
articles.summary: Apple TV is getting a section for watching video podcasts, just like Netflix and other streaming services.
articles.body: Apple’s streaming service will soon have a video podcasts section, the New York Times reports. It will start testing the feature in a developer release today, so expect a new update for iOS 27.3 beta testers to roll out in a few hours. Once it rolls out fully, the new video podcasts section will be available to everyone using an Apple TV device or app on all supported platforms. The expansion follows other streaming services’ push into podcasts. Netflix announced it was adding video podcasts to its platform last year, and debuted its first original video podcast series in January. Hulu and Disney Plus also offer podcasts, including a mix of companion podcasts for their shows and licensed podcasts like We’re Here to Help, hosted by Jake Johnson and Gareth Reynolds. Spotify has had support for video podcasts for several years now, and last year expanded them to its tvOS app. YouTube’s TV app has long been an option for watching podcasts, as well. Besides bringing its video podcasts to more screens, Apple is also planning to add more video podcasts to its regular Podcasts app, according to the Times. Apple added support for switching between audio and video podcasts in its iOS Podcasts app earlier this year, and added video podcasts on the tvOS Podcasts app in September.

articles.body: TRIGGER WARNING: This article includes references to sexual abuse.French actor Gérard Depardieu has decided to accept his sexual assault conviction and withdraw his appeal, bringing an end to his legal challenge against the verdict. The 77-year-old actor also issued an apology to the women who accused him of misconduct on a film set. His decision came on Monday, the day his appeal trial was scheduled to begin in Paris. Gérard Depardieu said he had accepted the court's judgment and acknowledged that his actions had caused harm.Gérard Depardieu accepts 18-month suspended sentence in sexual assault caseGérard Depardieu was convicted in May 2025 for sexually assaulting two women while filming 'Les Volets Verts' ('The Green Shutters') in 2021. The allegations involved a 54-year-old set decorator and a 34-year-old assistant working on the production. The court sentenced him to 18 months in prison, suspended, and ordered him to pay the two women a total of 29,040 euros in compensation and fines. It also directed that his name be entered into France's national sex offender database. The case became an important moment for the French film industry, particularly amid renewed discussions about workplace harassment and abuse of power following the #MeToo movement.Gerard Depardieu apologises, admits past behaviour had consequencesIn a written statement, Gérard Depardieu said he accepted the verdict and offered his "deep and sincere apologies" to those who may have suffered because of his conduct. He also reflected on his behaviour on film sets, admitting that he had often used provocative language and crude humour without considering its impact. The actor said he had believed his words and actions would not have consequences, but later understood otherwise. This new development indicates a departure from the actor’s previous stance in the initial trial in which he denied all accusations of sexual assault against him. He only acknowledged his use of inappropriate language and the grabbing of the hips of the set decorator while he was arguing.Gerard Depardieu faces another legal case amid controversyGérard Depardieu could be on the receiving end of another lawsuit in the coming months. According to information released in 2018, actress Charlotte Arnould accused actor Gerard Depardieu of raping her in his residence. The investigation judge had recommended that the case be brought to trial in August 2025. An appeal court in Paris will have to determine whether the case should proceed to trial. articles.title: Robert Pattinson named as the newest James Bond
articles.summary: Actor Robert Pattinson has been tapped to take on the role of James Bond as Amazon MGM Studios seeks to continue the blockbuster film franchise.
articles.body: Agent 007 has a new face. Actor Robert Pattinson has been tapped to take on the role of James Bond as Amazon MGM Studios seeks to continue the blockbuster film franchise. The studio announced the “Twilight” and “The Batman” alum as its choice to pick up the secret agent mantle, making the 40-year-old the latest in a list of leading men who have had the honor of playing the spy. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement, adding, “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.” The news comes after years of speculation over who would take over the role after Daniel Craig announced in 2019 that he was leaving the franchise. In the last week, rumors over Craig’s successor centered on Pattinson after a report from Puck suggested he was the front-runner. Denis Villeneuve is directing the new Bond film, which further fueled the speculation given that Pattinson collaborated with Villeneuve on the “Dune” franchise. The third installment of that franchise hits theaters in December. From starring in A24’s indie film “The Drama” to blockbuster epic “The Odyssey,” Pattinson has had a massive year, joining the handful of Hollywood stars who have dominated the big screen. Most recently, he starred as “Dateline NBC” alum Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” the A24 film that follows the TV personality’s “To Catch a Predator” era. The script for the new Bond film is being written by Steven Knight, who created the TV series “Peaky Blinders.” Amazon MGM Studios, the tech giant’s film unit, took over “creative control” of the James Bond series under a new deal with the franchise’s longtime producers, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The deal was announced in February 2025. Now, “Spider-Man” producer Amy Pascal and “Harry Potter” producer David Heyman will take on the latest installment, producing through Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films. In a statement, Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, emphasized that Pattinson’s casting is helping to “usher in a new era of Bond.” “This iconic character has captivated audiences around the world for more than six decades, and there’s no doubt that Robert’s remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice to carry that legacy forward,” he said, praising the “world-class creative team in place” that will be carrying on the franchise’s legacy. Bond fans have had many thoughts as to who would take on the mantle, with many hoping that Idris Elba would be tapped as the next British super spy. But Elba told People magazine in August that he was never truly in the race to become the next Bond. In recent months, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner reportedly also tested for the role. Bond has evolved into one of the most coveted roles for male actors in the United Kingdom. The book-to-screen character written by Ian Fleming has had a unique staying power across generations, beginning with Sean Connery in the 1962 film “Dr. No.” The Scottish actor played Bond across seven films and two decades. George Lazenby, the only Australian to play Bond, starred in 1969’s “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service.” He only played Bond for that film, which some have called one of the most underrated. Among the film’s fans is director Christopher Nolan, who called it his favorite of the franchise. But it was Roger Moore who was considered to be the one who replaced Connery in the iconic spy franchise. Moore was often criticized in comparison to Connery, but he was chosen to star in seven of the franchise’s movies. After Moore’s final Bond film in 1985, actor Timothy Dalton was given a smaller stint as the British agent. Dalton starred in two films, including “Licence to Kill,” in which he chose to portray Bond with a darker, more serious tone than previously seen by fans. The character took another turn when Pierce Brosnan was given the role. Brosnan said he grew up adoring both Connery and Moore in the role, telling GQ in 2014 that it never felt “real” to him that he held the job. Brosnan was told following his final Bond film, “Die Another Day,” that the character was being rethought and negotiations with his agent to continue his role had stopped. “And that certainly dug into the solar plexus of life, just because it was pretty gut-wrenching and because it had been somewhat heralded that I was coming back,” the Irishman told GQ. “So, it’s just business. And you’re the one caught in the crosshairs.” Brosnan was replaced by Craig, who was lauded by critics and fans alike after he made his 007 debut in the franchise’s “Casino Royale” installment. The actor chose to leave the fictional spy life behind after five films, saying on “The Graham Norton Show” in 2021 that he was glad to be leaving on his own terms even though it was an emotional decision. “I’m grateful to the producers for allowing me to do that,” Craig said. “But I shall miss it. I’ll probably be incredibly bitter when the new person takes over.” In a statement posted to X, Ian Fleming Publications, which owns and manages the literary rights to James Bond, praised the casting news. “As Bond himself reflects at the end of Moonraker when facing the fact that the object of his affections is engaged to another man, ‘He must play the role which she expected of him. The tough man of the world. The Secret Agent. The man who was only a silhouette.’ We look forward to Pattinson stepping into that silhouette and making it his own,” the account wrote. “We have no doubt that Ian Fleming would be amazed at the longevity of his creation and the fact that the world is still hungry for tales of the world’s greatest spy.​” Online, many diehard Pattinson fans — particularly millennials who identified as “Twihards” — were thrilled by the star’s newest role. “A great day for us Team Edward girlies,” wrote one X user, referring to Pattinson’s role as brooding, telepathic vampire Edward Cullen. Several users even posted a scene from the first “Twilight” film, released in 2008, in which Pattinson’s Edward is seen opening the car door for his romantic interest Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart) after one of their peers announces the school dance theme is Monte Carlo. “Gambling, tuxedos and Bond, James Bond,” one of the characters says, before it cuts to Pattinson and Stewart. “Twilight literally predicted Robert Pattinson being James Bond btw,” wrote one X user who shared the clip. Within minutes after the news dropped, many had also already cut thirsty fan edits compiling clips of the actor in his various roles and appearances. But there were many who blasted the choice. “robert pattinson as bond is such a boring choice man, please for the love of god choose an unknown,” one X user noted. And others who worried that Pattinson will be too busy with Bond for other roles. “we’re never getting that second Batman movie…” wrote one X user. “He’ll do great, I’m sure of it,” wrote another user. “But man am I still disappointed.”

articles.title: Robert Pattinson named the new James Bond, 'The Batman' star to take the 007 legacy into a new era: 'Dream come true is an understatement'
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond.
articles.body: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond. The actor was unveiled on Monday as the seventh star to play 007 and the first since Amazon MGM took charge of the legendary franchise. His casting puts an end to years of loud guesswork over who would take the role from Daniel Craig.Robert Pattinson calls James Bond role a dream come trueThe news comes during the longest break in 007 history. It arrives five years after ‘No Time to Die’ in 2021, the first Bond film in 64 years on screen to end with the hero’s death. Even so, the spy will return in the 26th Bond film, which Denis Villeneuve will direct.According to the Associated Press, Robert Pattinson said in a statement, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” “... To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”How Robert Pattinson won the roleRobert Pattinson joined the Bond rumour mill only recently, after it emerged that he had screen-tested for the part. Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult were also reportedly in the running. Many expected producers to pick a younger and less proven name. Instead, they went with one of the best-known actors of his generation. At 40, he is also fairly old to start as 007. He is currently filming another iconic role in ‘The Batman Part II’.From 'Twilight' to arthouse hitsRobert Pattinson already carries links to three mega-franchises: ‘The Batman’, ‘Twilight’ and ‘Harry Potter’. After his breakthrough in ‘Twilight’, however, he mostly chose independent, director-driven films. These include ‘Good Time’ with the Safdie brothers, Robert Eggers’ ‘The Lighthouse’ and Bong Joon Ho’s ‘Mickey 17’. Earlier this year, he earned rave reviews for playing a villain in Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’.Denis Villeneuve explains his choiceDenis Villeneuve admitted the decision was tough, but said it was the right one. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin,” the director said in a statement.Amazon takes over the Bond franchiseThe casting arrives at a key moment for the series. Amazon bought MGM, Bond’s longtime studio, for USD 8.5 billion in 2022. After lengthy talks over what to do with 007, producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson gave up creative control in 2025. The still-untitled Bond 26 is the first Bond film since 1962’s ‘Dr. No’ in which a Broccoli did not personally pick the spy.The job of finding a new Bond went to Amy Pascal, the former Sony Pictures chief and ‘Spider-Man’ producer, and David Heyman, the man behind ‘Harry Potter’ and ‘Paddington’. Steven Knight, known for ‘Peaky Blinders’ and ‘Locke’, has been brought in to write the script.The longest gap in Bond historyEven before Daniel Craig left the role, rumours and betting odds about his successor never stopped. Idris Elba, for one, has spent half his career brushing aside 007 talk. The Bond machine has rarely slowed down, yet the 26th film follows the longest absence ever. Since ‘No Time to Die’ finished principal photography in 2019, and its release was pushed back by the coronavirus pandemic, the real wait is even longer.What is at stake for 007Some fans doubt the new era. Mike Hopkins, head of the streaming giant and the studios, has promised to protect the franchise’s legacy and bring “the next phase in the legendary 007 for audiences around the world.”The stakes are huge, as the series, based on Ian Fleming’s novels, is among Hollywood’s most lucrative. The Bond films have earned more than USD 7 billion worldwide at the box office, and ‘No Time to Die’ alone brought in USD 774 million. The movie was released in cinemas in September 2021. The franchise also feeds other income streams, from streaming deals and video games to Aston Martin cars.Daniel Craig, little known before, was mocked at first as the first “blond Bond”, yet the role made him a household name.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.standfirst: Séptimo actor en protagonizar la saga más longeva y exitosa de la historia del cine
articles.summary: Séptimo actor en protagonizar la saga más longeva y exitosa de la historia del cine
articles.body: el proceso de elección del actor que sucederá a Daniel Craig como nuevo James Bond ha sido seguido con interés por los millones de seguidores del serial de películas más veterano y exitoso de la historia del cine (comenzó 14 años antes que Star Wars y, al menos hasta ahora, sólo tiene películas originales, sin excrecencias franquiciadas ni spin-offs). Pero no ha sido un proceso tumultuoso y polémico como el de la elección de la actriz que intepretaría a Scarlett O'Hara en 'Lo que el Viento se Llevó'. Finalmente la incógnita se ha despegado: el nuevo James Bond será Robert Pattinson. Y estará a las órdenes del director Denis Villeneuve. Es el séptimo actor que incorporará al agente secreto -con licencia para matar y al servicio de Su Majestad Británica- más famoso del mundo. Pattinson , de 40 años de edad, ha participado, entre otras producciones en la saga de Harry Potter, en 'Crepúsculo', en 'El Faro', en 'Tenet' , el Batman de Matt Reeves y en la tercera parte de la saga Dune, de modo que ya ha tomado parte tanto en películas de acción como en las que incorporan también personajes de cierta complejidad. Podría decirse también que su participación en 'Tenet' de Christopher Nolan puede valer como una suerte de 'ensayo general' dado que la obra era una especie de aportación apócrifa a la saga -Nolan había manifestado su interés por dirigir una película de la saga, pero EON Producciones no lo consideró oportuno- y, aunque no despertó entusiasmo entre incondicionales del director más popular del momento, sí resultó una muy correcta película de corte 'bondiano'. Algunas críticas señalaron que el elemento de ciencia ficción que incluía lo alejaba de la saga pero, la verdad, era una crítica poco consistente: el futurismo ha sido siempre una constante, de un modo o de otro, en las películas de Bond. Los actores que han interpretado a James Bond en el cine han sido Sean Connery (1962-1971), George Lazenby (1969), Roger Moore (1973-1985), Timothy Dalton (1987-1989), Pierce Brosnan (1995-2002) y Daniel Craig (2006-2021). Además, David Niven fue James Bond en la película Casino Royale de 1967, que no pertenece a la saga oficial aunque es de visión obligatoria. Ahora, la 'cátedra bondiana' pasará a juzgar si Pattinson puede estar a la altura de sus predecesores. El hecho es que la versatilidad del actor permite al menos darle un voto de confianza. Fue Sean Connery quien creó el modelo de personaje: un impecable asesino y seductor de mujeres al servicio del 'bien', capaz de salir airoso de situaciones desesperadas como el "¡¡¡No, señor Bond!!! ¡¡¡Espero que muera!!!" que le lanza Gert Frobe en 'Goldfinger' y que maneja con igual soltura la Walther PPK que cualquier otra herramienta letal, y que no desentona en el más elegante ambiente ni jugando a los chinos en un garito jamaicano como Daniel Craig. Se dice que el peligro de ser Bond es que te condena a una jaula dorada de encasillamiento. Eso alegó Sean Connery cuando abandonó por primera vez la serie, en 1968. Pero como sustituto, el modelo George Lazenby no funcionó, recuperó el papel y lo mantuvo hasta 1971. Su verdadero sucesor fue Roger Moore, famoso por la serie televisiva 'El Santo', que se mantuvo 12 años en el papel y lo dotó de un elegante sentido del humor en un contexto de películas que más parecían comedias de acción. En su tiempo el tono fue criticado pero su longevidad en el papel demuestra que siguió conservando el favor popular. Y se retiró por propia voluntad ("mis parejas en las películas no podrían ser mis hijas. También mis nietas"). Timothy Dalton no fue totalmente satisfactorio, aunque debió hacer frente a unas películas que extremaron la acción y la violencia. Pierce Brosnan, otro actor que venía de las series televisivas, retomó el camino correcto al componer un Bond que se ajustaba con naturalidad el nudo de la corbata mientras huía del acoso de los malos. Se juzgó a Daniel Craig cuando llegó como un error, porque en él se encontró a un Bond más amargado, más internamente violento y no precisamente guapo, como sus predecesores. Pero al final resultó estar al nivel de Sean Connery, pues es el único que ha tenido desarrollo como personaje en unas películas que, además, rediseñaban su relación con las mujeres (excepcional en este aspecto la aportación de Judy Dench como 'M') y hacían frecuentes guiños a los espectadores que llevan 50 años siguiendo a Bond. Así, queda esperar a ver cómo funciona Pattinson como Bond. Llega en un momento complicado: la serie ha pasado a manos de Amazon MGM después de haber dependido de sus creadores -EON Producciones- desde su inicio. El Bond que dejó Craig es un personaje ya complejo, más allá del elegante asesino despreocupado que interpretó Sean Connery, y su relación con las mujeres ya no es la de seductor-seducida al uso en el inicio de la serie en los 60 (y a este respecto hay que valorar la enorme importancia de Judy Dench como 'M' en sus películas). Y Bond debe enfrentarse a desafíos de nuestro tiempo: Connery y Moore alternaban asuntos propios de la Guerra Fría -en la que la relación de Bond con los soviéticos parecía más de amistosa competencia que de enemistad, recordemos que está condecorado con la Orden de Lenin-, Brosnan lidiaba con los problemas derivados del hundimiento del Bloque Soviético y Craig luchaba, sobre todo con corporaciones ocultas -la Spectra resucitada de las primeras películas- Pattinson tendrá otros desafíos. En fin. Esta vez no se ha discutido si Bond debe ser negro o debe ser una mujer (Grace Jones hubiera dado en su momento satisfactoria respuesta a ambos requisitos si se hubiese querido satisfacerlos). Veremos si el nuevo 007 -recordemos que recuperó su ordinal al devolvérselo Lashana Lynch- está a su altura. La Casa de Windsor le ha dado ya su aprobación. y eso es importante porque será la primera vez que Bond sirva a otro monarca: Carlos III. Todos los demás estuvieron al servicio de Isabel II. P.D: El autor reconoce que este artículo está escrito pensando en gente ya algo versada en la Saga Bond.

articles.title: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, says he gets threats after ‘You Can See Everything’
articles.summary: Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans, says that he loves the A24 documentary about his wife — despite the fact he says he now receives threats over his less-than-flattering depiction in the hit film.
articles.body: Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans, says that he loves the A24 documentary about his wife — despite the fact he says he now receives threats over his less-than-flattering depiction in the hit film. Evans spoke to CBS News’ “Sunday Morning” about the reception to Nathan Fielder’s “You Can See Everything,” as well as the backlash he’s received from viewers who felt that he came across as a villain. The film portrays Evans as possibly controlling and exploiting Holmes, but Evans said that he is not a monster who is “leveraging” the mother of his children. “It’s super painful, but me being angry about it doesn’t help change it,” Evans said. He also said that his family receives constant threats of violence, offering a recent example of a man screaming at him at a stop light while he was driving his kids to school. “And he is screaming the most vile things you have ever heard about: ‘I know where you live. I know who you are. I know where your kids sleep, and the things that I will do to you,’” Evans said. “And it was terrifying.” Holmes was convicted of four counts of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors the technology of her company, Theranos. The documentary by Fielder and Lance Oppenheim takes place in the months before Holmes reports to federal prison. Seyfried, who played Holmes in the 2022 limited series “The Dropout,” was among those who have been openly critical of Evans. In a Rolling Stone interview, Seyfried reflected on a tense dinner table conversation with Evans that was featured in Fielder’s documentary. She described Evans as “disrespectful” and “aggressive,” but also noted that she hadn’t built the rapport with him that Fielder had during the process. “I don’t like the way he’s using this human being, his wife — the person he says he’s ‘building monuments of love’ to — as a tool,” Seyfried said. “Maybe he does respect her, but he’s behaving like he does not respect her.” When asked about Seyfried’s role in the documentary, Evans said he was happy about Seyfried’s involvement because it showed the difference between the actor and the “real thing.” “And how eager she was to play a character,” Evans said of Seyfried. He added that he was glad Fielder was “there to help her” when asked about how well she played Holmes. “I’m going to do my best to not to speak poorly about other people right now, um, because I’ve had a lot of people do that about me recently and I know how it feels,” he said.
