articles.title: GTA 6 could make gaming history. Its mature rating should give parents pause.
articles.summary: We break down what parents should know about GTA 6's content, how to handle your child's "everyone else is playing" argument and where to set boundaries.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI is speeding toward release — and a full-on pop culture takeover.

The latest installment in Rockstar Games' blockbuster crime franchise arrives Nov. 19, with industry analysts predicting it will be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history. It has already generated an estimated $1 billion-plus in presales .

Amid the hype, parents may soon face a question: Can I play?

"What sets GTA apart is what the player is asked to do, not just what they see," says Jasmine Hood Miller, the director of family resources and content strategy for Common Sense Media, which provides age-based entertainment and technology recommendations for families.

The $80 game carries an M for Mature 17+ rating from the Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB). Before agreeing to the supersize download , here's what parents should know.

The franchise lets players step into the lives of criminals — stealing cars, carrying out robberies and using weapons. In GTA 6 , players control Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in the Florida-inspired state of Leonida, featuring Miami-esque Vice City.

Its mature content is central to the experience.

"GTA is one of the biggest game series in the world — and it was made for adults," Hood Miller says.

GTA 6's ESRB rating flags intense violence, blood and gore, nudity, strong sexual content, strong language and drug and alcohol use.

For context, Common Sense Media rated its 2013 predecessor, GTA V , for ages 18 and up. In that game, players kill gangsters, police officers and innocent bystanders, and one scene involves torture. Women are often portrayed as sexual objects, and none of the characters are positive role models, according to the organization's review.

Parents should also understand the distinction between GTA 6 and GTA Online. The former is a single-player game: Players follow its characters' stories and complete missions on their own. The latter is a separate multiplayer experience where players create their own criminal character, play with others and can spend real money on in-game currency. GTA 6 will not launch with an online component.

Why is the 'GTA 6' release such a big deal?

Geoff Keighley, the Game Awards creator and a gaming industry journalist, told the Hollywood Reporter , "I think GTA VI will be the biggest entertainment launch in history."

For starters, it's been 13 years since the last installment. Fans have been waiting — and kids who were too young to play when GTA 5 arrived may now be adults themselves.

The anticipation has translated into some big projections: The Hollywood Reporter cites a forecast of 45 million copies sold and $3.2 billion in sales in the game's first year. Research firm Circana reports that 29% of U.S. console and PC gamers plan to buy it, which would be the highest purchase intent recorded for a video game.

Some fans are making an event of it, canceling everything on their schedule to be among the first to play. Based on a survey, PCMag estimates that 12.5 million U.S. adults plan to take paid time off or adjust their work or school schedules to play. Logitech has even announced a dedicated day off for employees to play games.

What if your kid wants to play — and drops the dreaded 'but everyone else is'?

For many kids, this is their first GTA release, though they may already know the franchise through friends, older siblings or gaming videos. The appeal includes testing boundaries without real-world consequences and other in-game side activities, like racing and playing sports. Of course, participating in pop culture is a part of it too.

"GTA is a very well-made game that teens find fun to play," Hood Miller says.

Gaming is already a big part of their lives. A 2024 Pew Research Center survey found that 85% of U.S. teens ages 13 to 17 play video games. But familiarity with gaming doesn't necessarily mean readiness for GTA.

"Video games aren't one thing," Hood Miller says. "They're a medium, like movies or TV. A kid who plays Fortnite or Call of Duty is used to action. That doesn't mean they're ready for GTA any more than a kid who loves Marvel movies is automatically ready for an R-rated crime drama."

She points to the nature of the violence as one distinction.

"In GTA, players commit crimes, sometimes against ordinary people who did nothing wrong," she says. "The sexual content and the slurs are also much stronger than in most games kids already know."

If your child insists everyone else is allowed to play, Hood Miller recommends acknowledging the fear of missing out, even if the answer is still no. Check with other parents rather than assuming "everyone" has permission. If connecting with friends is the draw, help your teen find another title they can enjoy together.

While ratings describe the content, parents set the household rules. Hood Miller suggests considering three things: goals (what your teen wants from the game), guardrails (the concerns you want to address) and ground rules (the conditions for playing).

Start by watching gameplay together. How your teen talks about the violence, humor and portrayal of women will speak to whether they're ready.

She recommends approaching it "with curiosity rather than judgment," adding, "You can't guide a culture you're dismissing."

It's also a chance to discuss your family's values.

"GTA rewards things most families would never accept in real life," Hood Miller says. "Parents can ask their teen how that sits with them, and share where you stand and why."

Make your expectations clear before allowing play. Parents can use console settings to restrict games by age rating, require approval for purchases and set playtime limits. Check shared accounts too, so a child isn't accessing games through an adult's profile.

Those controls have limits, of course. Kids may encounter the game at a friend's or relative's house, making ongoing conversation as important as rules at home. The goal is to help them think critically about what they encounter, especially when parents aren't there.

"Teens who understand what their family cares about are better able to spot those messages in any game, show or app, and to decide what they're comfortable with," Hood Miller says.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson cast as James Bond: 'Batman' and 'Primetime' star to take over as 007
articles.summary: The 40-year-old will succeed Daniel Craig after a secretive search for the franchise's next actor.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson, the actor best known for his roles in The Batman and Twilight , has been named as the next James Bond following years of speculation and a secretive casting process.

Amazon MGM Studios announced Monday that the 40-year-old will take over the iconic role from Daniel Craig , who exited the spy franchise after 2021's No Time to Die . He reportedly beat out Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Nicholas Hoult and Josh O'Connor to secure the role.

The upcoming Bond movie, the 26th in the series, will be directed by Dune filmmaker Denis Villeneuve, while the script will be written by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight. The release date and title remain under wraps, but the BBC reported that the movie "is expected to go into production in 2027, before its release in 2028."

In a statement, Pattinson said, "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime."

He said he was "deeply grateful" to the team behind the movie "for their belief in me." He added, "To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team."

The U.K. Royal Family wrote on X , "Welcome to His Majesty's Secret Service, Mr Bond."

The actor is signed to a three-movie deal as Bond, according to a report by Puck .

Villeneuve said, "Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007.

"I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin."

Mike Hopkins, the head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, called Pattinson an "exceptional choice," praising his "remarkable range, magnetic screen presence and quiet intensity."

A short teaser video posted on social media showed Pattinson with a gun in hand, wearing a tuxedo, followed by the text, "James Bond will return." The caption read, "Identity Confirmed." A separate post read, "Robert Pattinson is James Bond."

The announcement comes exactly 20 years after Craig's first Bond movie, Casino Royale , was released in U.K. theaters.

The Hollywood Reporter said the casting process "was so secretive that Pattinson was only informed he got the role Sunday morning, by Villeneuve himself." The publication said the decision to hire the star "goes against conventional wisdom that Bond would go to a lower-profile actor." In contrast to Pattinson, Craig was not widely known when he was cast as the spy in 2005.

The estate of Bond author Ian Fleming said it was "delighted to welcome Robert Pattinson to the James Bond family."

Pattinson rose to fame in the Harry Potter and Twilight franchises in the 2000s, before stepping away from blockbusters to focus on independent films. He returned to big-budget filmmaking with Christopher Nolan's 2020 spy thriller Tenet , followed by his turn as Bruce Wayne in 2022's The Batman .

The actor has had a busy 2026, earning critical acclaim for his roles in The Odyssey , The Drama and Primetime. His next movie is Villeneuve's sci-fi epic Dune: Part Three , which hits theaters on Dec. 18, and he is currently shooting The Batman: Part II , due for release in February 2028.

Pattinson said in a 2012 interview with U.K. magazine Shortlist that he was "definitely" eager to play Bond in "20 years." He said, "I think there'd be nothing worse than, like, 'Let's get a fresh-faced Bond!' That would be the worst idea in the world. After Daniel Craig, you have to have some baggage. It would be ridiculous to reinvent [him] as some young posh kid. Or, if [he] was, I'd have to get so tortured in the first few scenes. I'd have to do the first film with one arm or something."

In a separate 2012 interview with ITV , Pattinson played down his chances. He said, "Why do people keep asking me this? There already is a James Bond! I don't know… I love James Bond, so I don't know."

He told the BBC in 2010, "[Those are] some big shoes to fill." He joked he would be a "pretty bad" Bond if he took on the role "right now."

The casting process was the first to be conducted without the involvement of the Broccoli family, which had overseen the Bond film franchise since its launch in 1962. The family announced in February 2025 that it would hand creative control to Amazon MGM Studios. The BBC said producers "clearly wanted a bankable name to lead the first iteration of Bond under Amazon's umbrella."

According to the official 007 website , screen tests for the role "are elaborate affairs involving hair and makeup, costumes, sets and other actors."

Craig starred as Bond across five films, beginning with 2006's Casino Royale . 2021's No Time to Die ended with the death of his version of 007.

His departure prompted frenzied speculation about his successor. Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Nicholas Hoult and Josh O'Connor all screen-tested for the role last month, according to multiple reports. Others linked to the role before the announcement included Jack O'Connell, Jacob Elordi, Theo James, Harry Styles, Jack Barton, Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Louis Partridge.

Hoult, who had also auditioned for The Batman , praised Pattinson for his role as the Dark Knight. "Rob did an amazing job with the character, and I loved seeing him in it," he said. "So I don't think I would have done as good a job as him ultimately. I don't think I could have fit as well into the world that Matt [Reeves] created as Rob did."

Asked by Variety in November 2024 whom he would like to see play Bond next, Craig replied: "I don't care."

The other actors to have portrayed Bond are Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan. Pattinson starred alongside Brosnan in the 2010 movie Remember Me .

The 25 Bond movies have grossed more than $7 billion worldwide in ticket sales, with No Time to Die collecting $774 million in 2021.
